html:
The transistor is a tiny electronic switch and amplifier made from a semiconductor. It is the basic building block of every computer chip, phone and modern electronic device.

The first working transistor was made in December 1947 at Bell Labs in New Jersey by John Bardeen and Walter Brattain, in a group led by William Shockley. The three shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1956.

Until then, electronics used vacuum tubes: glass bulbs that were large, fragile, hot and power hungry. Transistors were small, tough and cheap. By the late 1950s they were in pocket radios and hearing aids, and then in computers.

Shockley moved to California to start his own company. Eight of his engineers left to found Fairchild Semiconductor, the seed of Silicon Valley. There and at Texas Instruments engineers learned to put many transistors on one slice of silicon, the integrated circuit. The MOSFET type, made from 1959, became the most manufactured device in history.

That path led to the microprocessor, and today a single chip can hold billions of transistors.
sum: The transistor is a tiny electronic switch and amplifier made from a semiconductor. It is the basic building block of every computer chip, phone and modern electronic device.
